stemAssignment.source: No CP02 assignment exists for CIN_019; rift_finale music + river_shore ambience are the resolution cues (composed, CP26/CP30) for this scene (S01: wide three-quarter view of a mountaintop stone platform at dusk, five elemental pillars around an empty central space, WIDE_STATIC; S02: medium interior shot of a machinery hall, a young warden straining at a large sparking wall lever, a second warden at a bank of levers on a control console, MEDIUM; S03: wide dawn view of a riverside village under reconstruction, water cascading through a stepped, stone-repaired channel in the foreground, small groups of workers carrying logs and baskets, WIDE_STATIC; keyframes CIN_019 S01/S02/S03). rift_finale is the composed set's only full close -- the Ben Mua leitmotif's answering tail (F#-E-D), withheld in every other cue except the resolve stinger, sounds here -- for the line that closes the campaign's arc ('Lan nay khong ai giu het nam con duong.'). It has not been used in any scene mix before; this is its first scene-mix use. river_shore is the composed water-edge bed for the scene's landing: the spoken line sits in S03, at the rebuilt river village with the repaired channel running through the frame; also used for CIN_003 and CIN_008 (third scene-mix use). mountain_wind was passed over: it beds only S01's mountaintop -- neither the machinery hall nor the river village the line lands in. ben_mua was passed over: the rain-quay leitmotif of the opening (CIN_003/CIN_014) -- this scene is the answer to that opening, and the set reserves its full close for it. quiet_discovery was passed over: the exploration silence (CIN_007/CIN_011/CIN_016), wrong for a resolution. thang_long is the capital-city form (wrong setting); tran_son is the bell-led gate form (CIN_008/CIN_012); lam_trieu is the pastoral flute (CIN_009/CIN_013); sa_hoa is desert/dry (CIN_010/CIN_018); bach_uyen is the underwater low-passed form (CIN_015/CIN_017) -- the water here runs in an open repaired channel at dawn, not submerged; boss_mang_cot is boss material and there is no boss in this beat. underwater was passed over: a submerged bed, wrong for an open channel at dawn; wind_canopy is a forest bed; waterfall was used for CIN_009; rain_light and rain_heavy are rain beds, but no rain is depicted in any of the three keyframes (dusk platform, hall interior, dawn village); cave_drips is a cave bed; desert_wind, city_night, thang_long_crowd and forge are wrong for this setting; rift (the ambience bed) beds the rift site itself, not the village the scene lands in. The reveal stinger is the scene's only manifest-listed candidate stem (CIN_019_timing_v1.json).

notes: VO window 12.5-17.5 s is PROPOSED_ANIMATIC_PLACEMENT (only CIN_001_S05 is DECIDED); all 21 windows are approved for DRAFT VO per Goi 30 D1. The window is the uniform 12.5-17.5 s; it was NOT widened.

VO take runs 12.5-15.380 s: 2.880 s, ending 2.120 s BEFORE the 17.5 s window end -- the take FITS inside its window by 2120 ms (no overrun, unlike CIN_005/CIN_006/CIN_018). The take ends 2.620 s before the 18.00 s scene end, so no tail trim at the scene edge. The window, the take and the timing are unchanged.

The CP17 VO take measures -25.52 LUFS (checkpoint 17, re-verified from real bytes this run) -- one of the quietest campaign takes (the CIN_008 take measured -23.10 LUFS). VO is kept at unity per the recipe, not normalized.

Staging: the timing manifest records the S03 dialogue onscreen: true for Ly An (NPC_LYAN), and the keyframe manifest lists Ly An among the scene's on-screen characters -- but S03's frame is a WIDE dawn view of the whole village under reconstruction (stepped, stone-repaired channel in the foreground, small groups of workers carrying logs and baskets): no individual figure is identifiable as Ly An at this scale, and the scene's faces and costumes are storyboard placeholders (NPC_LYAN has no approved cinematic character lock). The placement is onscreen per the timing; the identity is not verifiable in the frame -- a final-picture/character-lock matter, not a mix defect; the mix does not move the VO.

Ducking depth is measured on the ducked bus against its unducked render (RMS over the full VO window vs a 2 s reference before the window). The full-window method from checkpoint 39 is retained so the depth is comparable across the CIN_003/CIN_005/CIN_007/CIN_008/ CIN_009/CIN_010/CIN_011/CIN_012/CIN_013/CIN_014/CIN_015/CIN_016/CIN_017/CIN_018/CIN_019 mixes (a 2 s slice can understate the cut on cues whose window opening is quiet).

Ducking depth is measured from real bytes over the full VO window (CP39 method, same params as every scene mix); rift_finale carries real signal inside this window (segment RMS -22.1 dBFS measured from the stem bytes this run), so a real cut is expected here, and the number in the manifest is the measured one, not a target. If the depth came out 0.0 dB it would mean the cue is silent in this window -- that is NOT the case for rift_finale (unlike quiet_discovery in CIN_016, which is digitally silent 12-15 s); a 0.0 dB reading here would be investigated, not reported as a silence pocket.
Ambience loop join uses a 1 s acrossfade; loopQA reports the max sample jump at the join against the bed's own 99.9th-percentile jump.
Stinger placement at 6.0 s (S02 start) is PROPOSED pending picture lock, mirroring the CIN_004 reveal at 6.0 s.
